label: database-row-insert-clean-vault
notes: The first baseline captured against a vault that is not full of the
leftovers of measuring. 850 files of perf debris were removed first — 13
abandoned perf databases and the old shared table that had grown to 358
rows — taking the index from 743 records to 3.
That drop is also a controlled experiment, and it settles a hypothesis:
the write's slope is NOT about how big the vault is. Emptying it moved
nothing that matters. mutate still goes 33ms -> 67ms across the table
(1.98x/2.04x/2.05x, against 34 -> 68 and 2.00x on the dirty vault), and the
overall growth ratio still sits at 1.52-1.60 against 1.54.
Only the read-back shrank: query's last quarter went 10ms -> 4ms, which is
the one place vault size was actually being paid.
So the slope belongs to the table's own row count. Combined with the
in-handler measurement — the server handler grows 18ms -> 28ms over the
same span, while the client observes 33 -> 67 — roughly 24ms of the 34ms
of mutate growth happens outside the request handler, on a vault with
three records in it. It is therefore not background indexing contention
either; both of the obvious server-side explanations are now excluded.
What has NOT been excluded, and is the next thing to measure: the client
measures a request as `performance.now()` inside the fetch `.then()`
callback, so any delay in the main thread getting round to that callback
lands inside the number. The scenario adds one row per iteration to a
table React re-renders, so the main thread has strictly more to do on each
successive sample. That would make part of this 'slope' a rendering cost
being attributed to the write.
Two server-side hypotheses were killed by measurement before this one:
the shadow-repo git commit (zero WIP commits fire during a 40-insert run —
that path is driven by Y.Doc persistence, not row writes), and response
serialization (Zod validation plus JSON is 0.1ms and does not grow; the
payload only goes 1.6KB -> 2.6KB).
rowInsertMedianMs is submit -> the first read-back that started after the
write landed. Runs are only comparable at the same iteration count.
Captured with OK_PERF_ROW_ITERATIONS=40. IMPORTANT: the dev server serves
/api from packages/server/dist, not from src — run
`bun run --filter @nedian0brien/synapsenote-server build` and restart
before measuring a server change, and grep dist to confirm it landed. An
earlier run of this scenario measured a bundle that did not contain the
change under test.
